To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the lateral distribution of coherent radio pulses from air showers can be calculated from the shower parameters and the radio signal from a cosmic-ray induced air shower contains information on the chemical composition of the primary cosmic rays.
the lateral distribution function of coherent radio emission from air showers is a very sensitive measure for the mass composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic-rays.

(1) the LDF for radio pulses emitted from air showers can be calculated in a macroscopic description, (2) the LDF is determined by the pancake function at small distances from shower axis and by the shower profile function at large distances, (3) the LDF can be used to discriminate between showers induced by different primaries, (4) due to interference between different contributions to the radiation the pattern of the intensity is not circular symmetric.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the theoretical basis for the interpretation of radio signals from cosmic ray air showers.
the development of the radio technique as a method for cosmic-ray physics and for the detection of ultra-high-energy neutrinos.
the development of new methods to detect and to study ultra high-energy cosmic rays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LDF is determined by the longitudinal shower profile and the shower age at the observer.
the LDF for coherent radio emission from air showers is very sensitive to the mass composition of the cosmic rays.
the LDF for coherent radio emission is a very powerful tool for the determination of the chemical composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic-rays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to calculate the LDF of coherent radiation from air showers and we have shown how this could be used to discriminate between the composition of cosmic rays at the highest energies.
the LDF of coherent radio emission from air showers is a very powerful tool to determine the chemical composition of cosmic rays.
the radio technique is a very promising method to measure the mass composition of cosmic rays in the energy range from 10^17 to 10^20 eV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
radio detection of air showers can provide an important tool to determine the chemical composition of cosmic rays.
the LDF is determined by the longitudinal shower development, which is different for proton and iron showers.
the LDF is a very promising method to determine the chemical composition of the cosmic rays.
